title: ModelQuotaAccounts
description: GET /v1/quota[?model=<id>] — per-account quota snapshots for the accounts serving a model, or for all accounts when the parameter is omitted. Auth: inference API key (Bearer). The 'model' parameter is optional; 'model_id' is accepted as an alias. Thinking suffixes (e.g. 'model(high)') are stripped before lookup. Data: live provider quota APIs first (60s TTL cache, stale fallback on errors), degrading per account to passive local snapshots when live is unavailable. ?refresh=live forces a live fetch; ?refresh=cached serves passive snapshots only. The body is a JSON array of accounts sorted by provider then name; operator-disabled accounts are excluded. Status codes: 200 (this schema, min 1 item), 401 bad key, 404 no serving account (no credentials available when the parameter is omitted), 503 auth manager unavailable. Errors are {"error": string} (see $defs/error), matching the v1 auth envelope. Compatibility: additive-only under /v1 — new optional fields may appear, existing fields never change type or meaning; clients MUST ignore unknown properties and tolerate absent optional fields. Grouping (à la CPAMC provider tabs) is done client-side on 'provider'. NOT stable: plan strings, status vocabulary behind in_cooldown, and masking affix lengths; 'description' is reserved for future use.

provider.description: Raw provider key (e.g. codex, claude, meta, gemini, vertex). Group by this for CPAMC-style provider tabs; gemini-family keys stay distinct, exactly as CPAMC badges them.

provider_name.description: Displayable formatted provider name (e.g. Codex, Claude, Gemini, xAI, Z.AI, OpenCode, Kimi). Derived from provider; absent when the provider key is empty.

name.description: Masked account email only (e.g. 'o***@example.com'). Metadata/attributes email wins; a label that is itself an email covers hand-made files with no email field. Final fallback is the masked auth filename stem with any .json suffix excluded. Never a full email, key, or path. Absent when neither email nor filename is known.

type.description: 'oauth' for OAuth-style credentials, 'api' for API-key credentials.

plan.description: Subscription plan display label when known (live provider data first, local signals as fallback). Opaque string, absent when unknown.

description.description: Reserved for future use. Currently never present.

in_cooldown.description: True while the account (credential or requested-model state) is effectively blocked by a cooldown.

windows_observed_at.description: RFC 3339 time 'windows' was produced: live fetch time when live data backs the account, else the newest passive observation. Absent when nothing was ever observed.

windows.description: Normalized usage windows: live provider data first, passive snapshots on fallback (credential- and model-level merged, model wins per name). Always an array, possibly empty. Deterministically ordered (5h, 7d, monthly, then alphabetical).

reset_credits.description: Spendable manual resets, soonest first. Length is the count. Absent when the provider reports none. Codex is the only provider CPAMC surfaces this for; window refresh times stay on windows[].reset_at.

name.description: Stable window slug. Well-known: '5h' (codex five-hour, claude 5h), '7d' (codex weekly, claude 7d), 'monthly' (codex team secondary), 'daily'/'weekly' (devin). Grouped limits prefix their group: antigravity model groups ('gemini-models/5h'), claude model limits ('opus/7d', 'sonnet/7d', 'cowork/7d', 'oauth-apps/7d', 'fable/7d'), zai meters ('credits/5h'), xai products ('product/<slug>'), namespaced codex limits ('bengalfox/7d'). Codex windows are classified by duration (18000s/604800s/28-31d), falling back to primary/secondary position.

used_percent.description: Consumed share of the window, 0-100. Absent when upstream reported no usage figure.

reset_at.description: RFC 3339 window reset time. Absent when unknown.

status.description: Opaque per-window status when reported (e.g. claude 'allowed'). Absent otherwise.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant this reset stops being spendable.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason. Match on HTTP status, not text.
